# LeafIT Environment

Apply Ponytail and i-have-adhd from [repository instructions](../../copilot-instructions.md) throughout. Read the [README](../../../README.md) for the immediate foundation/enabler TODO and longer-term showcase goals: Windows 365, Windows 365 for Agents, AVD, AVD Hybrid, Windows 365 Link, Intune, and primarily Defender for Endpoint. AVD Hybrid is a distinct product, not shorthand for hybrid join or an assumed Azure Local deployment; verify its own architecture and prerequisites before implementation. Keep each scenario portable to an eligible clean tenant, with explicit bootstrap and per-scenario acceptance/repeat-apply tests. A TODO is not deployment approval, and a recommendation or export is not evidence of a working rebuild.

Always use the [CAF naming convention guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/ready/azure-best-practices/resource-naming) and CAF abbreviations. Do not reintroduce a bespoke naming pattern or fixed five-group layout. Choose resource groups from lifecycle, ownership, and access requirements and create them only when needed. Follow the README's foundation design; public DNS must survive workload rebuilds, and zone creation, registrar NS/DS changes, and Entra verification are separate operations.

The shared foundation uses the `infra` workload identifier and one shared group where ownership, access, and lifecycle align. Organize definitions as top-level workload/group, then service: `infra/main.bicep` owns the reviewed group naming input, resource-group declaration, and composition; child modules such as `infra/dns/zone.bicep` receive that group scope and own only their service resources. Separate modules do not imply separate groups. Do not create empty future-service folders or add a redundant environment token. Refresh private inputs, compiled artifacts, and previews after changing names or entry points; never delete the shared group for a scenario reset.

## Scope And Privacy

Keep tenant-specific inputs and private commercial information only in ignored `.env`, never in this skill, memory, public examples, output, or documentation. Keep minimized target inventory and deployment evidence in ignored `private/`. Check that both locations are ignored and untracked; preserve existing values unless authorized. Do not execute `.env` as code or display its contents.

Operate only on the configured LeafIT target. Validate the authenticated context against private expected tenant and subscription IDs and fail closed on mismatch. Explicitly approved interactive work can use `Connect-AzAccount -UseDeviceAuthentication` with private `TARGET_TENANT_ID` and `TARGET_SUBSCRIPTION_ID`, process-scoped context and disabled autosave; follow [Target Sign-In](../../../README.md#target-sign-in). Do not create an application or certificate just for this path. Unattended certificate authentication additionally requires populated `TARGET_CLIENT_ID` and `TARGET_CERTIFICATE_THUMBPRINT` plus an accessible private key in the execution account's certificate store. Never fall back to unprefixed legacy settings or an unrelated cached session. Azure RBAC and Graph application consent are separate grants; verify both privately. Successful sign-in does not prove write access.

The repo is the single source of truth for desired state. All preflight, preview, apply, and verification use the target only. Read-only preflight does not authorize consent grants, application creation, license changes, policy changes, or deletion.

## Regions And Prerequisites

Use Sweden Central (`swedencentral`, CAF naming component `swc`) by default for Cloud Endpoint compute, AVD session hosts, supported Azure infrastructure, and Windows 365 Azure network/VNet scenarios. Germany West Central (`germanywestcentral`, `gwc`) requires an explicit current constraints/SKU/quota/capacity review; never silently fall back. West Europe and North Europe are not standard choices. Intune is not controlled by an Azure-region input; public DNS remains global while its group/deployment metadata uses the selected region. These are project choices, not universal service-availability guarantees. Refresh names, private parameters, compiled artifacts, and previews after a regional change.

Always execute approved repeatable changes through versioned automation. [Initialize-Prerequisites.ps1](../../../infra/Initialize-Prerequisites.ps1) handles only the currently implemented Microsoft.Network dependency. In the retained authenticated target PowerShell process, run it without switches for read-only preview/readback, with `-Apply` for separately approved registration, or with `-CheckOnly` for offline checks. It parses required private fields without executing them, verifies target context and subscription ownership, and checks the location catalog (not product/SKU availability). Registered is a no-op; Registering is pending without another request. Verify Registered and a NoChange repeat apply before declaring this prerequisite complete. Do not register unrelated providers, grant access, deploy resources, or alter Graph/registrar settings as a side effect. Never deploy a placeholder verification TXT or stale preview.

For DNS mail/service records, keep source inventory in ignored `private/dns/records.json` and deploy through `infra/Deploy-Foundation.ps1` plus the Bicep service module. Merge existing apex TXT/MX values, fail closed on conflicting CNAME targets, preview owned record-set operations, and verify each record and TTL. The Azure deployment does not change registrar delegation or verify the Entra domain.

## Domain-Controller Deployment And Resume

Use PowerShell 7.6 on Windows, the private input/dependency checks, and [identity/Deploy.ps1](../../../identity/Deploy.ps1). Default invocation previews; `-Apply` requires selected-workload approval. `-ResourcesOnly` stops before guest promotion; `-DnsOnly` performs only the reviewed guest DNS refresh. `-OperationsOnly` previews the scheduling migration; adding `-Apply` updates only Automation and its scheduler permissions without provisioning VMs, promoting AD, refreshing guest DNS, or starting backup jobs. It requires existing Protected/Healthy backup protection and last-backup Completed status, not a fresh application-consistent recovery point. The full-deployment freshness gate and backup configuration remain unchanged. Stop any previous local apply with explicit approval before resuming; never overlap applies or infer script completion from an ARM deployment alone.

Preserve Standard backup policy and use protected-item API `2025-01-01` for this Trusted Launch definition; the vault explicitly declares `publicNetworkAccess: 'Enabled'`. Do not silently migrate to Enhanced policy or remove backups to bypass a gate. The optional `identity/Initialize-Prerequisites.ps1 -PublicIpFeature` is only for the specific Azure BYOIP-feature rejection; registration still needs approval and ready-state readback.

Keep the immediate demo milestone small: public DNS, two working DC VMs, and automatic weekday startup. Use the existing Automation account for power control with plain `VmName1` and `VmName2` parameters, exactly two bindings (06:00 Start and 18:00 Stop), and VM-scoped permissions without guest Run Command access. Preserve existing networking, security, and backups. Do not add scheduled AD diagnostics, runtime-smoke jobs, publication-only modes, or binding-snapshot frameworks to satisfy this milestone. One real scheduled start plus a basic AD/DNS check is the demo acceptance test; forest recovery and clean-tenant reproducibility remain separate claims.

Use native draft-content upload and verify content, published state, and the existing `DcPowerShell76`/Az `15.1.0` runtime without changing its kind. Send schedule starts as UTC with `Europe/Brussels` recurrence. An older JSON/Health deployment needs `-OperationsOnly -RetireHealthSchedule` preview and separate approval before adding `-Apply`. Migration refuses active jobs or shared schedules, pauses owned schedules, replaces their bindings around publication, retires Health, and only then resumes Start/Stop. Existing schedule definitions are skipped during the template deployment so pausing is preserved; failures attempt to leave owned schedules paused. Incremental deployment alone does not retire Health. Do not publish the new contract alone or treat local preparation as a live migration. What-if defaults/expressions are not actual-state drift evidence.

## Workflow

1. **Preflight:** confirm the requested TODO item, required inputs, target identity, permissions, licensing, capacity, and dependencies using least-privilege reads. Follow pagination and mark denied or unsupported reads as unknown, not absent. Do not start snapshot jobs, install tenant apps, or broaden permissions without checking the side effects and authorization.
2. **Choose Ownership:** give each resource or setting one owner. Use Bicep for Azure; Graph PowerShell for supported Entra/Intune settings; Graph Bicep only for suitable supported Entra resources; NMe MCP for Nerdio-owned objects. Verify actual Nerdio tool schemas and the vendor-supported Hydra deployment method. Consider Microsoft365DSC only when it eliminates substantial custom reconciliation; do not introduce a framework speculatively.
3. **Define:** write reviewed, sanitized desired state into native templates or JSON. Keep tenant IDs and private inputs separate; resolve target dependencies using stable logical keys and fail on ambiguous matches. Define only owned properties. Use the licensing skill for minimum eligible bundles and required add-ons. Pin tested tool/API versions and explicitly identify beta or manual dependencies.
4. **Preview And Apply:** compare live target state with the repo's desired state before applying. Azure what-if does not cover Graph Bicep resources. Require explicit approval for deletions, replacements, and tenant-wide lockout risks. Preserve emergency access; start new Conditional Access policies report-only. Apply in dependency order with bounded handling for throttling, eventual consistency, and asynchronous jobs. Never blindly retry non-idempotent creates or delete unmanaged objects.
5. **Verify:** read back owned target properties and assignments, test workload behavior, prove a no-change repeated apply, and rehearse a clean rebuild using only versioned definitions and private target inputs. Keep recovery instructions and evidence private unless fully generic. State which checks passed and which remain unverified; end with one next action.

## Nerdio Boundary

MCP is the transport, not the source of truth. Every Nerdio change must have a sanitized desired-state definition, discoverable tool mapping, dependency order, and readback check. Do not let Bicep, Graph, and Nerdio fight over the same host pool, policy, schedule, or assignment. If the installed MCP lacks an operation, record the gap and request a supported alternative; do not silently bypass the chosen owner or fall back to browser automation.

## Recovery Boundary

Configuration recreation does not restore user data, preserve service-generated object IDs or device trust, or recover passwords and MFA registrations. Backup and recovery require separately authorized work.

No cloud deployment scripts or pipelines are required merely to record the backlog. Add them when implementing an explicitly requested, testable workload.
